sections.h2: How does selling a house in Lake in the Hills work?
sections.html:
Three paths are open to an owner: hire an agent, handle the sale yourself, or sign with an investor who pays cash and skips the repair list. Whichever route you pick, a sale in Lake in the Hills runs through the same local pieces: Village Hall for permits and contractor questions, the three fire protection districts and four school districts that overlap the village, and the McHenry County Recorder for the deed.

Lake in the Hills sits in McHenry County, northwest of Chicago, along the Randall Road corridor. The 2020 census counted 28,982 residents, and that number has barely moved since. A seller here is usually working with a house built after the 1990s growth wave, or with an older lakeside cottage in the east side of the village, and the two behave very differently at sale time.

sections.h2: How did Lake in the Hills grow into the village buyers see?
sections.html:
It is a former summer-cottage community that turned into a commuter suburb. A federal judge started the lakeside settlement around Woods Creek Lake in 1923, vacationers from Chicago slowly became year-round residents, and the village was formed on November 29, 1952. Growth exploded in the 1990s: roughly 17,000 people were added in that decade, and the village issued more than 1,000 residential building permits in 1995 alone.

Randall Road now splits the village into an older East Side and a newer West Side, and Algonquin Road marks the boundary with the village of Algonquin. Buyers tend to compare houses by subdivision, so it helps to know which one yours belongs to.

  • The Old Section: four older neighborhoods (Original, Indian, Tree and Presidents, named for their street themes) near the lake, with mixed architecture instead of tract styling.
  • Boulder Ridge: a gated community north of Algonquin Road with the village's only 18-hole golf course.
  • Big Sky and Harvest Gate: early subdivisions west of Randall Road, split by Woods Creek and close to the village hall and Lincoln Prairie Elementary.
  • Spring Lake Farm: an early-1990s subdivision south of Miller Road with both single-family and multifamily housing.

sections.h2: Which school and fire districts cover a Lake in the Hills address?
sections.html:
Four school districts share the village, so the district tied to your street matters to many buyers. Consolidated District 158 covers most of the dense western half, District 300 covers the older eastern sections, and Elementary District 47 and Community High School District 155 reach a small central slice.

That means a seller on the west side may market Huntley High School, while a seller on the east side points to Jacobs High School in Algonquin, and the central pocket feeds Crystal Lake South and Crystal Lake Central. Elementary names in the village include Lake in the Hills Elementary, Lincoln Prairie, Glacier Ridge, Canterbury, Woods Creek, May Chesak, Hannah Martin, Mackeben and Marion Conley, depending on the boundary.

Fire service is also split. The village says three separate districts, the Algonquin-Lake in the Hills Fire Protection District, Crystal Lake Fire Rescue and the Huntley Fire Protection District, serve different parts of town, each with its own taxing authority. Check your tax bill or call the district before you describe the house in a listing.

sections.h2: What does federal data say about homes in Lake in the Hills?
sections.html:
Census Bureau QuickFacts describes a village of owners: more than four in five households own their home. Population was estimated at 28,590 in July 2025, a dip of 1.4 percent from the 2020 starting point.

With nearly three people per household and more than a quarter of residents under 18, three- and four-bedroom floor plans are the common fit. A commute near half an hour fits the Randall Road drive toward Interstate 90, which the village puts about seven miles south.

sections.h2: Do you need a permit before selling a Lake in the Hills house?
sections.html:
No permit is needed just to sell, but any construction, remodeling that changes structure, plumbing, electrical or heating, and many replacements need one first. Village Hall at 600 Harvest Gate reviews both zoning and building code before a permit issues, and the Village Hall number printed on its permit page is 847-960-7400.

  • Applications can be emailed as PDFs to the community development address, dropped in the box at the Village Hall parking lot entrance, or brought in person.
  • Air conditioners, furnaces, roofing, siding, water heaters and water softeners can be permitted through the online portal.
  • Contractors must be licensed by the village; call Village Hall to confirm a name before hiring.
  • Plumbing inspections are offered Monday, Tuesday and Thursday from noon to 4 p.m.
  • Village approval does not depend on your homeowner association, so check the association separately.

If a past owner finished a basement or deck and you cannot find the permit, ask Village Hall what is on file for the address before a buyer's inspector asks. A buyer paying cash for the house as-is may accept that risk, but a lender-backed buyer often will not.

sections.h2: Which village rules show up on a showing day?
sections.html:
Winter and noise rules are the ones sellers trip over. The village plows most streets, aims to clear them 6 to 10 hours after snow stops, and bans on-street parking once an inch has fallen under Municipal Code Section 41.03. County crews handle roads such as Algonquin, Lakewood, Randall and Ackman, and the state handles Routes 31 and 47.

Property owners clear their own sidewalks and driveways, and snow belongs in the yard, not the street. Garbage cans go to the curb at 6 p.m. or later the evening before pickup and should be stored out of sight otherwise. Construction, lawn work and personal snow removal are exempt from the noise limits only between 7 a.m. and 8 p.m., which matters if you are rushing repairs before listing.

sections.h2: What happens at recording and transfer in McHenry County?
sections.html:
Deeds are filed with the McHenry County Recorder, and the state transfer tax under 35 ILCS 200/31-10 is fifty cents per $500 increment of the value written on the declaration. Under 35 ILCS 200/31-25 the paperwork is due with the deed or inside three business days of the transfer, whichever comes first, with a seller's and a buyer's signature (or those of their agents).

The county's own checklist for good recordings is worth reading before closing:

  • The online MyDec declaration must read "Closing Completed."
  • A deed needs the grantee's address and the full McHenry County legal description.
  • A Plat Act affidavit must accompany a deed that uses a metes and bounds description.
  • A signed exemption paragraph or a PTAX-203 or MyDec declaration must come with every deed.
  • Documents need a half-inch clean margin and a clear 3 by 5 inch space in the upper right corner.

Ask the McHenry County Recorder whether a county or village transfer fee applies to your parcel, since this brief covers only the state rate.

sections.h2: When does a cash offer fit a Lake in the Hills sale?
sections.html:
A cash sale makes sense when the house needs work a lender's appraiser would flag, when you inherited a home you cannot maintain, or when the calendar matters more than squeezing out the top price. Houses with deferred maintenance, an association dispute or a pending violation notice are typical examples, since each can slow a conventional listing.

Compare any offer against a listing by asking the buyer to state the closing date, who pays recording and transfer charges, and whether repairs are priced in. Get that in writing, then confirm the title company will handle the PTAX declaration and the recorder submission.

faqs.q: What if my Lake in the Hills house has open permits?
faqs.a: Yes, but expect the buyer or title company to ask about them. Contact Village Hall at 600 Harvest Gate to see what is open for the address, then either finish the inspections or disclose the work. A cash buyer may take the house with the open item priced in.

The McHenry County Recorder records deeds for Lake in the Hills. The county's recording checklist requires a completed transfer declaration, the grantee's address and the full legal description, and the MyDec record must show that closing was completed.

faqs.q: Do homeowner associations affect permits here?
faqs.a: Village approval is based on codes and zoning, not on your association. Many Lake in the Hills subdivisions still have their own rules, so get any needed association sign-off in addition to the village permit.

faqs.q: Who handles snow removal on my street?
faqs.a: It depends on the road. The village clears most local streets, county crews handle Algonquin, Lakewood, Randall and Ackman Roads, the state handles Routes 31 and 47, and some roads belong to property owner associations. Call 847-960-7500 for a specific street.

faqs.q: How is the state transfer tax stated?
faqs.a: The state sets the tax in 35 ILCS 200/31-10 and applies it to the value shown on the declaration. A deed that says it conveys the property subject to a mortgage lets the unpaid mortgage balance be left out of the base.
